<h2 class="tagline"><strong>NSHipster</strong> is a journal of the overlooked bits in Objective-C, Swift, and Cocoa. Updated weekly. </h2>

<section id="latest">
<article>
<header>
<small>This Week...</small>
<h1 class="title">
<a href="/metrickit/">Metric​Kit</a>
</h1>
</header>
<p>At WWDC this year, Apple announced a coordinated effort between Xcode 11 and iOS 13 to bring new insights to developers about how their apps are performing in the field.</p>
<a class="readmore" href="/metrickit/">Continue Reading</a>
</article>
</section>
<section id="recent">
<h1>Recent Articles</h1>
<ul>
<li>
<a class="title" href="/swiftui-previews/">Swift​UI Previews on macOS Catalina and Xcode 11</a>
<p>Working on a large iOS codebase often involves a lot of waiting. But with Xcode 11, our wait is finally over — and it’s all thanks to SwiftUI.</p>
</li>
<li>
<a class="title" href="/ios-13/">iOS 13</a>
<p>To mark last week’s release of iOS 13, we’re taking a look at some obscure (largely undocumented) APIs that you can now use in your apps.</p>
</li>
<li>
<a class="title" href="/apns-device-tokens/">Apple Push Notification Device Tokens</a>
<p>Precedent plays an important role throughout software engineering. So what does a change in iOS 13 to push notification registration have to say about Apple’s API design decisions?</p>
</li>
<li>
<a class="title" href="/dark-mode/">Dark Mode on iOS 13</a>
<p>After waiting for what felt like an eternity (but was only, like, a year),  Dark Mode is now finally coming to the iPhone and iPad iOS 13. But will your app be ready on launch day?</p>
</li>
<li>
<a class="title" href="/identifiable/">Identifiable</a>
<p>Swift 5.1 gives us yet another occasion to ponder ontological questions and weigh in the relative merits of various built-in types as stable identifiers.</p>
</li>
<li>
<a class="title" href="/accessibility-keyboard/">macOS Accessibility Keyboard</a>
<p>Beyond its immediate usefulness as an assistive technology, the Accessibility Keyboard challenges us to think differently about the nature of input methods and any remaining distinction between mobile and desktop computers.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</section>
